title: Your first minute in the Hall
promise: Start a concert and take the music with you.

steps.title: Begin with Satie
steps.text: Press Play to hear the First Gymnopédie. The next recording follows automatically. Space pauses; N and P change pieces when no control has focus.

steps.title: Watch the score
steps.text: Choose Score, then touch a bar to hear it; the gold highlight follows the recording.

steps.title: Choose your programme
steps.text: Open the programme to choose an evening or a single recording. The full concert follows composers’ birth order, keeping movements of a work together.

steps.title: Return to the music
steps.text: Close the programme; the music keeps playing. The question-mark button brings you back to this tour.

steps.title: Take the music with you
steps.text: This player stays with you across the site. Open a chapter or lesson and keep listening.

title: Read a score by listening
promise: Watch Satie’s Gymnopédie unfold on the page.

steps.title: Let the piano begin
steps.text: Press Play to start the First Gymnopédie.

steps.title: Choose Score
steps.text: Follow the gold highlight across the printed bars.

steps.title: Find the score’s source
steps.text: The caption names the score and explains the timing. Timings are aligned automatically and await checking by ear. Touch a bar to hear it.

steps.title: Try Notes
steps.text: Choose Notes to see each voice in a different colour, with pitches and lengths taken from the score.

title: Five ways to see the music
promise: Explore Beethoven’s Fifth through its score, instruments and returning themes.

steps.title: Start Beethoven’s Fifth
steps.text: Press Play; you can change views while the recording continues.

steps.title: Score: the printed page
steps.text: Choose Score to follow the gold highlight through the bars.

steps.title: Notes: separate the voices
steps.text: Choose Notes to see the score’s pitches and note lengths as coloured lines.

steps.title: Orchestra: the players
steps.text: Choose Orchestra to see each instrument group light up as it plays. You can try this view with Boléro too.

steps.title: Form: hear the returns
steps.text: Choose Form to see the sections and the arcs joining returning themes. Touch a section to hear its opening.

steps.title: Sound: inside the recording
steps.text: Choose Sound to see the recording’s frequencies and loudness, alongside an estimate of its harmony.

steps.title: Fill the Hall
steps.text: Press F or use this corner button to enlarge the view; press F again to return.

steps.title: Keep listening as you read
steps.text: Open a chapter or lesson while the concert continues; this bar lets you pause from any page.

title: Hear how a section turns
promise: Hear the silence before Beethoven’s horn call and see how the score prepares it.

steps.title: Open The joins
steps.text: The joins explain the turns between sections: a silence, a new chord, a change of instrument.

steps.title: Hear the first join
steps.text: Replay the passage leading into the silence before the horn call.

steps.title: Find the diamonds
steps.text: Select a diamond on the timeline to hear the passage around a join.

steps.title: Return to As it plays
steps.text: Choose As it plays for notes that follow the recording, including a card at each join.

steps.title: Open How we know
steps.text: Open the note’s sources to see what comes from the score, the recording or a historical account.

title: Find a recording’s story
promise: Find the session, the source and a citation you can use.

steps.title: Open This recording
steps.text: Find the performers, session, original disc and digital transfer in the recording tab.

steps.title: Read the evidence labels
steps.text: Documented facts have a cited source; inferred ones are reasoned from evidence. Disputed entries give alternatives, and unknown dates stay unknown.

steps.title: Find other performances
steps.text: Open a comparison of the same music; each card identifies its performance and transfer.

steps.title: Cite this recording
steps.text: Copy the citation with the performer, recording source and Hall link.

steps.title: Take the sources with you
steps.text: Download the recording register as CSV or JSON, with separate fields for facts, evidence labels, sources and alternatives.

title: Change hands, keep the phrase
promise: Switch between Rachmaninoff’s 1919 and 1928 recordings mid-phrase.

steps.title: Choose the 1919 recording
steps.text: Select the Edison performance: its clock is the reference for this comparison.

steps.title: Start the recording
steps.text: Press Play at the listening desk; switching cards will take you to the matching place in another recording.

steps.title: Move into the phrase
steps.text: Move to 42 seconds in the reference recording, beyond the opening lead-in.

steps.title: Switch to 1928
steps.text: Choose the electrical Victor remake and hear the phrase continue.

steps.title: Read the tempo map
steps.text: Above 1×, the performer takes longer over the same music than the reference; below it, less time.

steps.title: Compare a short passage
steps.text: Choose a passage to hear it in each available performance, one after another.

title: Follow the Dies irae
promise: Trace the chant’s path to Rachmaninoff’s Isle of the Dead.

steps.title: One tune, several afterlives
steps.text: Choose Dies irae to trace the chant through the web; each gold line opens a connection and its sources.

steps.title: Hear the chant’s outline
steps.text: Play the synthesised opening; the caption explains the chosen rhythm and tempo.

steps.title: Follow it to Rachmaninoff
steps.text: Open the Isle of the Dead connection to see where the chant enters Rachmaninoff’s music.

steps.title: Read the connection’s history
steps.text: The evidence note explains how we know Rachmaninoff used the chant.

steps.title: Read and share
steps.text: Open a source to read further, or copy the page address to share this connection.

title: From Vivaldi’s violin to Bach’s organ
promise: Hear how Bach transcribes Vivaldi’s opening.

steps.title: Put the works side by side
steps.text: Vivaldi’s Concerto RV 522 becomes Bach’s organ transcription BWV 593.

steps.title: Hear the violin line
steps.text: Play the first violin’s opening two bars in A minor, using synthesised sound.

steps.title: Hear the organ line
steps.text: Now play Bach’s uppermost line; the caption names the omitted voices and links to the full score.

steps.title: Read the full scores
steps.text: The sources take you to the works behind these short examples.

title: Find a place in time
promise: Explore Vienna in 1900, then follow Mahler from place to place.

steps.title: Set the year
steps.text: The Map opens at 1900; drag the year slider to move through time.

steps.title: Follow Mahler
steps.text: Mahler is selected; the numbered list gives dates and sources for each place on his map.

steps.title: Hear music from a place
steps.text: Play a work linked to this place, or choose another recording by the composer.

steps.title: Explore Vienna’s composers
steps.text: Open Encounters to find composers whose dates overlap in the selected city.

steps.title: Read the city’s records
steps.text: Explore the dates and sources, then use Find a city to visit another place.

title: Let a story lead the listening
promise: Explore Vienna in 1900 through music and paintings.

steps.title: Begin Vienna 1900
steps.text: Press Begin; the music carries you from station to station, and you can pause to read or look at a painting.

steps.title: Read beside the music
steps.text: Each station pairs a recording with a story and an exhibit; short notes appear as the music plays.

steps.title: Open the sources
steps.text: Find this excerpt’s times, its sources and a link to the full recording in the Hall.

steps.title: Turn to the next station
steps.text: Choose Next or a numbered station; after this tour, the arrow keys work too. Your place is saved for next time.

title: Read, trace, cite
promise: Explore Mahler’s chapter, follow his borrowings and cite the page.

steps.title: Find your way round
steps.text: Use the contents to jump to Mahler’s life, music, works, places or sources.

steps.title: Follow the influences
steps.text: Open a connection in the Web of Influence to read its story and sources.

steps.title: Choose something to read
steps.text: Each book, catalogue and article has a short note to help you choose.

steps.title: Cite this page
steps.text: Open a Chicago reference or BibTeX entry for this page.

steps.title: Copy the citation
steps.text: Copy the Chicago citation and set the access date to the day you read the page.

title: Find the word you heard
promise: Hear sonata form, open a definition and search the Atlas.

steps.title: Put a term to music
steps.text: Explore sonata form through Beethoven’s Fifth, with links to related terms and passages.

steps.title: Hear the example
steps.text: Choose Hear it to play the passage described in the caption.

steps.title: Open a quick definition
steps.text: Hover over an underlined term, reach it with Tab or tap it to open a definition; follow its link for more.

steps.title: Search from any page
steps.text: Use Search or press / to find composers, works, recordings, ideas and guide lessons. On a small screen, look inside Menu.

title: Hear what changes on return
promise: Compare Beethoven’s exposition and recapitulation, bar by bar.
feature: Return Lab · paired passages · bar charts

steps.title: Hear the first statement
steps.text: Choose A to hear the marked passage from the exposition.

steps.title: Hear its return
steps.text: Choose B to hear the corresponding passage as Beethoven brings the music towards the home key.

steps.title: Read the bar grid
steps.text: Matching bars share a column; colours separate the voices, and hatched gaps mark bars with no counterpart.

steps.title: Compare score and performance
steps.text: Read Beethoven’s written changes beside the time each bar takes in this performance.
